findings: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is delivered on subsequent parent-thread death; if parent and ancestor subreapers have already terminated at installation, it is not delivered. A launch-race guard is required for a design relying on this API.
Parent-death setting is cleared in forked children and privileged exec/credential transitions; ordinary exec retains it. Any descendant-spawn assumptions need explicit scope.
An alive ancestor marked child subreaper can adopt orphan descendants, receive SIGCHLD and actually wait on them. Parent-death signalling alone does not provide a historical wait acknowledgment.

Python documents preexec_fn as unsafe with threads; start_new_session performs setsid in the child and process_group performs setpgid. A robust implementation must respect these boundaries rather than infer process-tree cleanup from a direct child wait.
